# Part III: The System Architecture {.unnumbered}

Part III walks the canonical five-stage handoff sequence that transforms raw physical observations into certified actuator setpoints, plus the physical silicon substrate that hosts them. Where Part II explored how policies are trained, Part III details the runtime architecture that executes them across heterogeneous hardware in real time.

Each chapter in Part III owns exactly one stage of the pipeline: what representation it consumes, what mathematical transformation it performs, what expiration lease it attaches, what rejection test protects its output boundary, and how it hands execution forward to the next stage.

### The Six Pillars of Part III

Part III steps sequentially through the complete runtime pipeline:

* **Chapter 8: Perception (*What Perception Hands Over*):** Ingests raw transducer streams (photons, pulses, magnetic fluxes), manages sampling integration latencies and bus bandwidths, bounds spatial measurement error, and emits calibrated, timestamped sensory observations.
* **Chapter 9: Memory (*What Memory Hands Over*):** Fuses observations across time and multi-modal reference frames, maintains belief distributions through dynamic occlusions, bounds the rate of state uncertainty decay, and emits structured world states with explicit epochs.
* **Chapter 10: Intent (*What Intent Hands Over*):** Translates high-level task descriptions and linguistic prompts into expiring geometric proposals, evaluating task feasibility, workspace reachability, and lease durations before passing goals forward.
* **Chapter 11: Planning (*What Planning Hands Over*):** Generates dynamically feasible, continuous reference trajectories from expiring geometric goals, resolving temporal chunk seams and trajectory continuity across receding planning horizons.
* **Chapter 12: Enforcement (*What Control Hands Over*):** Operates as the deterministic safety filter, implementing Control Barrier Functions, safe set projections, and minimal intervention laws that hold exclusive authority over physical motor setpoints.
* **Chapter 13: Placement (*Two Paths on One Die*):** Analyzes the physical silicon partitioning and on-die co-location of slow, stochastic model inference and hard real-time safety enforcement, characterizing memory crossbar contention, thermal coupling, and worst-case execution time ($R = C + B + I \le D$).

### What You Will Master in Part III

By the conclusion of Part III, you will understand the complete end-to-end systems architecture:

1. **The Contract at Every Boundary:** Every stage of the pipeline produces an explicit output record with mandatory metadata: timestamp, coordinate frame, calibrated uncertainty, and lease duration.
2. **Deterministic Invariant Filtering:** How Control Barrier Functions ($h(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0$) and safe sets provide formal guarantees of forward invariance while allowing high-capacity learned policies full expressiveness within safe envelopes.
3. **Silicon Independence:** Proving that real-time enforcement loops retain their sub-millisecond execution deadlines even when co-located on a shared system-on-chip with memory-saturating neural accelerators.
